IPE Wood Floor

Natural strength. Lasting beauty.

01

Overview

About IPE Wood Floor

IPE is one of the densest hardwoods used for decking. Its tight grain and natural oils make it resist moisture, insects and heavy wear, so it suits pool decks and terraces that face sun and rain every day.

Premium IPE hardwood is dense, weather resistant and naturally rich in colour. A top choice for decks that face sun, rain and heavy footfall.

Enquire about thisSee all types
02

Types & quality

Choose the right IPE Wood Floor

Swatches are digital renderings that show the look of each type. The real product's colour and finish can vary a little.

Pool decks

Natural IPE (fresh)

Freshly milled boards show warm reddish-brown tones with a tight grain. Usually sold smooth or reeded for grip.

Best for: Pool decks, terraces

Visible decks

Oiled IPE

A UV-protective oil deepens the colour to a rich dark brown and slows weathering. Re-oil once or twice a year.

Best for: Visible decks, premium homes

Modern

Weathered grey IPE

Left unoiled outdoors, the surface turns silver-grey. This is only a colour change, the timber stays strong.

Best for: Modern, natural-look gardens

07

Material guide

Know your material

What it is

IPE, often called Brazilian walnut, is a very dense tropical hardwood. Its tight grain makes it hard, heavy and naturally resistant to decay.

How it is made

Logs are milled into boards, kiln-dried and surfaced. We recommend buying from certified, legal sources.

Installation tip

Pre-drill every screw, use stainless steel fixings and leave small gaps between boards for drainage and ventilation.

Strengths

  • Very hard and long lasting
  • Naturally resists rot and insects
  • Rich brown colour with a premium look

Good to know

  • Heavy, so cutting and drilling need good tools and pre-drilling
  • Turns silver-grey in sun unless oiled
08

FAQ

Common questions

Does IPE get hot in the sun?

Dark boards warm up in direct sun, but they usually feel more comfortable than stone or concrete.

Will it fade?

Sunlight slowly turns it silver-grey. A UV oil applied regularly keeps the original tone.

09

Care & maintenance

Easy to look after

  1. 01

    Rinse with water and a soft brush to remove dust.

  2. 02

    Apply a UV-protective oil once or twice a year to keep the colour warm.

  3. 03

    Leave it unoiled if you prefer a natural silver-grey ageing.
